source_text: perductum enim illum ad Pilatum onerare coeperunt, quod se regem diceret Christum, sine dubio (dei filium sessurum ad dei dexteram). ceterum alio eum titulo grauassent, incerti an filium se dei dixisset, (ni)si ('uos s dicitis* sic pronuntiasset, hoc se esse, quod dicerent. Pilato quoque interroganti: tu es Christus? proinde: tu dicis, ne metu potestatis uideretur amplius respondisse, (respondit.) Constitutus est igitur dominus in iudicio — et statuit in iudicio populum suum; ipse dominus in iudicium uenit cum presbyteris et archontibuspopuli, secundum Esaiam — atque exinde omne scriptum passionis suae impleuit: tumultuatae suntibidem nationes et populi meditati suntinania; adstiterunt reges terrae etarchontes congregati sunt in unum aduersus dominum et aduersus Christum eius: \'nationes\' Romani qui cum Pilato fuerant; \'populi\' tribus Israhelis; (reges) in Herode, (archontes) in summis sacerdotibus. nam et Herodi uelut munus a Pilato missus Osee uocibus fidem reddidit. de Christo enim prophetauerat: et uinctum eum ducent xenium regi. delectatus est denique Herodes uiso Iesu nec uocem ullam ab eo audiuit. tamquam agnus enim ante tondentem sic non aperuit os suum, quia dominus dederat illi linguam disciplinae, ut sciret, quando eum oporteret proferre sermonem, illam scilicet linguam, quam in psalmo adglutinatam gutturi suo tunc probabat non loquendo. Et Barrabas quidem nocentissimus uita ut bonus donatur, Christus uero iustissimus ut homicida morti expostulatur. sed et duo scelesti circumfiguntur illi, ut inter iniquos scilicet deputaretur. uestitum plane eius a militibus diuisum partim, (partim) sorti concessum Marcion abstulit respiciens psalmi prophetiam: dispertiti sunt sibi uestimenta mea et in uestitum meum sortem miserunt. aufer igitur et crucem ipsam. idem enim psalmus de ea non tacet: foderunt manus meas et pedes. totus in illo exitus legitur: circumdederunt me canes, synagoga maleficorum circumuallauit me. omnes, qui spectabant me, naso inridebant me; locuti sunt labiis et capita mouerunt: sperauit in deum, liberet eum. quo iam testimonium uestimentorum? habe falsi tui praedam: totus psalmus uestimenta sunt Christi. Ecce autem et elementa concutiuntur. dominus enim patiebatur ipsorum. ceterum aduersario laeso caelum luminibus loruisset, magis sol radiis insultasset, magis dies stetisset, libenter spectans pendentem in patibulo Christum Marcionis. haec argumentata quoque mihi competissent, et si non fuissent praedicata: caelum, inquit Esaias, uestiam tenebris; hic erit dies, de quo et Amos: et erit die illa, dicit dominus, occidet sol meridie — habes et horae sextae significationem — et contenebrabit super terram. scissum est et templi uelum, angeli eruptione derelinquentis filiam Sionis tamquam in uinea speculam et in cucumerario casulam.s o quantum perseuerauit etiam tricesimo psalmo Christus ipsum reddere! uociferatur ad patrem: ***, ut et moriens ultima uoce prophetas adimpleret. hoc dicto expirauit. quis? spiritus semetipsum an caro spiritum? sed spiritus semetipsum expirare non potuit. alius est qui expirat, alius qui expiratur. si spiritus expiratur, ab alio expiretur necesse est. quodsi solus spiritus fuisset, discessisse potius diceretur quam expirasse. quis igitur expirat spiritum nisi caro, quae et spirat quando illum habet et ita eum cum amittit expirat? denique si caro non fuit, sed phantasma carnis, phantasma autem spiritus fuit, spiritus autem semetipsum expirauit et expirando discessit, sine dubio phantasma discessit, cum spiritus, qui erat phantasma, discessit, et nusquam comparuit phantasma cum spiritu. nihil ergo remansit in ligno, nihil pependit etiam post expirationem, nihil de Pilato postulatum, nihil de patibulo detractum, nihil sindone inuolutum, nihil sepulcro nouo conditum? atquin non nihil. quid ergo illud fuit? si phantasma, adhuc ergo inerat et spiritus. si discesserat spiritus, ergo abstulerat phantasma. superest impudentiae haereticae dicere phantasma illic phantasmatis remansisse; sed scilicet Ioseph corpus fuisse nouerat quod tota pietate tractauit, ille Ioseph, qui non consenserat in scelere Iudaeis, beatus uir, qui non abiit in consilio impiorum et in uia peccatorum non stetit et in cathedra pestium non sedit.
pass_a_gloss: For they began to load him, brought to Pilate, because he was saying that he is the Christ, the King, without doubt, the Son of God, who will sit at the right hand of God. However, they would have burdened him with another title, uncertain whether he had said that he is the Son of God, unless, as you say, he had pronounced that he is what they were saying. Also, when Pilate was questioning him: 'Are you the Christ?' then he said: 'You are saying it,' so that he might not seem to have responded further out of fear of power. Therefore, the Lord was established in judgment, and he stands in judgment of his people; the Lord himself came into judgment with the elders and the rulers of the people, according to Isaiah. And from then on, every scripture of his passion was fulfilled: the nations were tumultuous and the peoples meditated on vanities; the kings of the earth stood and the rulers were gathered together against the Lord and against his Christ. For 'nations' are the Romans who were with Pilate, 'peoples' are the tribes of Israel, 'kings' are in Herod, and 'rulers' are in the high priests. For even Herod, as if a gift sent by Pilate, gave his testimony with the words of Hosea. For the prophet had prophesied about Christ: 'And they will lead him bound as a gift to the king.' And Herod was delighted to have seen Jesus, but he did not hear any voice from him. For just as a lamb before its shearer, so he did not open his mouth, because the Lord had given him the tongue of discipline, so that he might know when he ought to bring forth a word, that tongue, namely, which in the psalm he was proving to be glued to his throat, not speaking. And indeed, Barabbas, a most wicked man, was given as a gift as if he were good, but Christ, the most just, was handed over to death as if he were a murderer. But also, two wicked men were crucified around him, so that he might be counted among the wicked. His garment, divided by the soldiers, was partly given over to lots, but Marcion took away the fact that it was divided, looking back at the prophecy of the psalm: 'They divided my garments among themselves and cast lots for my garment.' Therefore, take away also the cross itself, for the same psalm does not remain silent about it: 'They pierced my hands and my feet.' The entire outcome is read in it: 'The dogs surrounded me, the assembly of the wicked enclosed me.' All who were looking at me were mocking me with their noses; they spoke with their lips and moved their heads: 'He hoped in God, let him free him.' What is the testimony of the garments now? Have the spoils of your false ones: the entire psalm is the garments of Christ. Behold, even the elements were shaken, for the Lord was suffering. However, if the adversary had been injured, the heaven would have grown dark with shadows, the sun would have insulted with its rays, the day would have stood still, gladly looking at Christ hanging on the cross of Marcion. These arguments would have been sufficient for me, even if they had not been predicted: 'The heaven,' says Isaiah, 'will become a garment of darkness'; this will be the day, of which also Amos says: 'And it will be on that day, says the Lord, the sun will set at noon' - you have also the signification of the sixth hour - 'and it will grow dark over the land.' The veil of the temple was torn, and the angels, abandoning the daughter of Zion, left her like a watchtower in a vineyard and like a hut in a cucumber field. Oh, how much Christ himself fulfilled the thirtieth psalm! He cries out to the Father, so that, even in dying, he might fulfill the prophets with his last voice. Having said this, he expired. Who expired? The Spirit himself or the flesh the Spirit? But the Spirit could not expire himself. There is another who expires and another who is expired. If the Spirit is expired, it is necessary that he be expired by another. And if he were only Spirit, it would be said that he departed rather than expired. Who, therefore, expires the Spirit, if not the flesh, which also breathes when it has it and thus expires it when it loses it? Finally, if the flesh was not, but a phantom of flesh, and the phantom was Spirit, and the Spirit expired himself and departed by expiring, without doubt the phantom departed, since the Spirit, which was the phantom, departed, and the phantom did not appear anywhere with the Spirit. Therefore, did nothing remain on the wood, did nothing hang even after the expiration, was nothing asked of Pilate, was nothing taken away from the cross, was nothing wrapped in a shroud, was nothing placed in a new tomb? But indeed, something did. What was it, then? If it was a phantom, therefore the Spirit was still in it. If the Spirit had departed, therefore he had taken away the phantom. It remains for the impudence of the heretic to say that the phantom of the phantom remained there; but certainly Joseph knew that it was a body, which he handled with all piety, that Joseph, who did not consent to the crime of the Jews, a blessed man, who did not go in the counsel of the impious and did not stand in the way of sinners and did not sit in the chair of the pestilential ones.

pass_b_english: They began to heap charges on him once he was brought before Pilate, because he claimed to be the Christ, the King — and, beyond doubt, the Son of God, who will sit at God's right hand. They would have saddled him with a different title, unsure whether he had actually said he was the Son of God, unless, as you put it, he had declared that he is exactly what they were accusing him of being. When Pilate questioned him, 'Are you the Christ?' he answered, 'You say so,' so that he would not appear to have said more out of fear of authority. The Lord was therefore installed in judgment — and he takes his stand to judge his people; the Lord himself comes into judgment with the elders and rulers of his people, according to Isaiah (Isaiah) — and from that point on every scripture of his passion was fulfilled: the nations were in an uproar and the peoples plotted in vain; the kings of the earth took their stand and the rulers gathered as one against the Lord and against his Christ (Psalm). 'Nations' means the Romans who were with Pilate; 'peoples' means the tribes of Israel; 'kings' points to Herod; 'rulers' points to the chief priests.

Even Herod, sent by Pilate as if he were a gift, bore witness in the words of Hosea (Hosea). For the prophet had foretold about Christ: 'And they will lead him bound as a gift to the king.' Herod was delighted to see Jesus, yet he heard not a single word from him. Like a lamb before its shearer, he did not open his mouth, because the Lord had given him a tongue of discipline, so that he would know when he ought to speak — that tongue, I mean, which in the psalm he proved was stuck to his throat by not speaking (Psalm). Barabbas, a thoroughly guilty man, was granted life as if he were good, while Christ, the most righteous, was demanded for death as if he were a murderer. Two criminals were crucified alongside him, so that he would be counted among the wicked. His clothing was divided by the soldiers, partly by lot, but Marcion has stripped away the fact of the division, looking back at the psalm's prophecy: 'They divided my garments among themselves and cast lots for my clothing' (Psalm). So take away the cross itself as well, for the same psalm does not keep silent about it: 'They pierced my hands and my feet' (Psalm). The whole outcome is read there: 'Dogs surrounded me, a gang of evildoers encircled me' (Psalm). All who stared at me mocked me with their noses; they curled their lips and shook their heads: 'He trusted in God, let him rescue him' (Psalm). What testimony do the garments offer now? Take the spoils of your false ones: the entire psalm is Christ's garments.

Look, even the elements were shaken, for the Lord was suffering. But if the adversary had been wounded, heaven would have draped itself in shadows, the sun would have insulted with its rays, the day would have stood still, gladly watching Marcion's Christ hanging on the gibbet. These arguments would have sufficed for me even if they had not been foretold: 'The heavens,' says Isaiah, 'will become a garment of darkness' (Isaiah); this will be the day of which Amos also says: 'And on that day, says the Lord, the sun will set at noon' — you have the significance of the sixth hour as well — 'and it will grow dark over the land' (Amos). The temple veil was torn, and the angels, abandoning the daughter of Zion, left her like a watchtower in a vineyard and like a hut in a cucumber field (Isaiah). Oh, how thoroughly Christ himself fulfilled the thirtieth psalm! He cries out to the Father, so that even in dying he might fulfill the prophets with his last voice (Psalm 30). With those words he breathed his last. Who breathed his last? The Spirit himself, or the flesh the Spirit? But the Spirit could not breathe his last on his own. There is one who expires and another who is expired. If the Spirit is expired, he must be expired by another. And if he were only Spirit, it would be said that he departed rather than expired. Who, then, expires the Spirit, if not the flesh, which also breathes while it has him and so expires him when it loses him? Finally, if there was no flesh but a phantom of flesh, and the phantom was Spirit, and the Spirit expired himself and departed by expiring, then beyond doubt the phantom departed, since the Spirit, which was the phantom, departed, and the phantom appeared nowhere with the Spirit. So nothing remained on the wood, nothing hung even after the expiration, nothing was asked of Pilate, nothing was taken down from the cross, nothing was wrapped in a shroud, nothing was laid in a new tomb? But indeed, something did. What was it, then? If it was a phantom, then the Spirit was still in it. If the Spirit had departed, then he had taken the phantom away. All that remains for the heretic's impudence is to say that a phantom of a phantom remained there; but Joseph certainly knew it was a body, which he handled with all reverence — that Joseph, who did not consent to the crime of the Jews, a blessed man, who did not walk in the counsel of the impious, did not stand in the way of sinners, and did not sit in the seat of the pestilential (Psalm).

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the complex theological arguments regarding the reality of Christ's flesh versus a phantom, preserving the distinctions between 'expirare' (to breathe one's last) and 'expirari' (to be expired/breathed out). All scripture citations in Pass B are correctly identified and added as required (e.g., Isaiah, Hosea, Amos, Psalms). The translation of the difficult section regarding the 'tongue of discipline' and the 'phantom' is faithful to the Latin syntax.
